questions.q: How does Sivers structure his book about how to live?
a: He gives 27 conflicting philosophies, each argued as correct
He interviews 27 people about their daily routines
He summarizes 27 religions in historical order
He offers one method with 27 practical steps
questions.why: The overview says each chapter claims to have the perfect answer, and the reader must decide which fits right now.

questions.q: Why does Sivers present contradictory advice?
a: To show that no single philosophy fits every season
To prove that most self-help advice is wrong
To make the book longer and more thorough
To confuse readers into buying another book
questions.why: Lesson one says the contradictions reveal that life is gray, with no one right answer that lasts forever.

questions.q: Which everyday question does Sivers use to illustrate life's grayness?
a: What do I feel like eating today?
What should I do with my career?
Who do I want to become this year?
How much money do I really need?
questions.why: Lesson one says your answer changes from morning to night, showing how preferences shift and contradict themselves.

questions.q: What three life themes does the summary group Sivers's chapters into?
a: Focus, freedom and curiosity
Love, work and legacy
Health, wealth and wisdom
Faith, family and service
questions.why: Lesson two maps the chapters onto small and focused, open and independent, and big and immersed approaches.

questions.q: What does Sivers say about switching life themes?
a: It is normal and necessary, but you should notice it
It is a sign that something has gone wrong
It should happen only once in a lifetime
It is possible only when you are young
questions.why: Lesson three says life themes change with the season, and awareness lets you make those shifts deliberately.
